actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 400 - 7 (Roll no. 234). (text: CR H4394-4395)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.

Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H4394-4395)

dimensions.assessment: Involves federal officials, emergency managers, state, local, Tribal, territorial officials, and private sector and community stakeholders participating in an exercise.
dimensions.evidence: How the effects of a successful terrorist attack against critical infrastructure could be mitigated by emergency managers, State officials, and appropriate private sector and community stakeholders.

dimensions.assessment: Mandates the development and execution of an emergency response exercise and subsequent reporting of findings and legislative recommendations.
dimensions.evidence: Secretary of Homeland Security... shall develop and conduct a collective response to terrorism exercise

dimensions.assessment: No specific appropriations or funding changes are stated in the source text.
Directs a federal agency to execute a specific preparedness exercise scenario and submit a detailed after-action report to congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 60 days after the completion of the exercise required under subsection (a), the Secretary of Homeland Security shall... submit to... Congress an after-action report

dimensions.assessment: Focused on a single required exercise and a subsequent one-time after-action report submitted within 60 days of completion.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 60 days after the completion of the exercise required under subsection (a)

missing_information: The specific cost of conducting the exercise and any long-term legislative changes that might emerge from the findings.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the Department of Homeland Security to conduct a specific terrorism response exercise focusing on extreme cold weather events and cascading critical infrastructure failures, followed by an after-action report to Congress.
